policy.resident_core: Rust. Long-lived Ninja services, contracts, orchestration and agent-facing tooling should not require a Python runtime.
policy.external_tooling: Use mature tools in their native implementation. Wrap capabilities; do not rewrite crawlers, browsers, archives or statistical packages merely to make them Rust.
policy.python_boundary: Python is permitted only behind isolated batch adapters when a scientific or data tool materially benefits from the Python ecosystem. It is not the resident Ninja core.

tools.role: Historical web corpus and index before recrawling live pages.
tools.notes: Prefer archived historical material when it satisfies the experiment and preserves point-in-time evidence.
Discovery output is not evidence until acquired and preserved through a reproducible collector.

tools.role: Current-topic and narrative reconnaissance across multiple public sources.
tools.notes: Reconnaissance only. Never use synthesized Last30Days output directly as a market feature.
Persist retrieval provenance and distinguish source timestamps from retrieval/first-seen quality.

tools.role: Efficient HTTP acquisition with browser-like TLS/HTTP behavior where ordinary HTTP is insufficient.
tools.notes: Use before paying browser-process cost when possible.

tools.role: Crawler frontier, sessions, concurrency and retries.
tools.notes: Benchmark against Scrapy for the first real acquisition workload instead of running two crawler frameworks by default.

tools.role: Mature high-throughput crawling and extraction pipelines.
tools.notes: Candidate workhorse when its mature pipeline model is a better fit than Crawlee.

tools.role: Normal browser automation for JavaScript-heavy public pages.
tools.notes: Browser acquisition is escalation, not the default for every URL.

tools.role: Hardened Chromium-compatible browser path when normal automation is blocked or misclassified.
tools.notes: Use as a specialized fallback; record challenge/failure rates by source.

tools.role: Independent Firefox-derived browser engine for acquisition diversity.
tools.notes: Maintain engine diversity without making an experimental browser the only acquisition path.

tools.role: Specialized Chromium challenger for difficult public web acquisition.
tools.notes: Benchmark success rate, latency and maintenance burden before promotion to a default path.

tools.role: High-fidelity browser crawling and WARC/WACZ capture for replayable web evidence.
tools.notes: Use selectively for evidence that may change or disappear; do not archive the entire web by default.

tools.role: Main-content extraction from articles and HTML pages.
tools.notes: Preserve raw capture/hash independently from extracted text.

tools.role: Structured parsing of PDFs, tables and complex documents.
tools.notes: Use OCR only when a usable text layer is unavailable.

tools.role: Local analytical engine over Parquet/Silver/Gold data.
tools.notes: Preferred analytical substrate before introducing a resident database service.

tools.role: Dataset and artifact lineage tied to Git revisions.
tools.notes: DVC metadata belongs in Git; large data does not. Remote configuration comes after the first canonical dataset is selected.

tools.role: Backtest/runtime compatibility check for artifacts promoted into Master Trader.
tools.notes: Do not use Freqtrade as a substitute for E1/E2 statistical validation.
Experiment records must reference the exact code commit used.

tools.role: Build and test the resident Rust Ninja core/tooling.
tools.notes: Rust is the primary implementation language for resident Ninja software.
